extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy, and writers interested in representing time, movement, and duration
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and philosophical criteria for representing movement, duration, and change (becoming) instead of treating them as discrete static states; useful for theorists and creative writers seeking to portray lived time. Emphasizes placing thought/description within duration rather than reconstructing motion from snapshots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install yourself within duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not 'approach' duration from outside; to think true duration you must 'install yourself within it straight away.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the principal prescriptive point: instead of trying to reconstruct movement from external, discrete views, place consciousness within the flow so you grasp both change itself and the successive states as potential immobilities. Anti-pattern: treating movement as a sequence of detached static states (the 'cinematographical' approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the cinematographical mechanism for portraying becoming
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary knowledge and language operate like a cinematograph: they take 'snapshots' (qualities, forms, acts) and reconstitute movement by stringing them on an abstract 'becoming in general.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: this practical, discontinuous method is useful for action but inadequate for speculating on real becoming. Example/anti-pattern: portraying a continuous motion merely as a rapid sequence of static images (film-like snapshots) while assuming movement is reducible to those images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reduce movement to a series of states
rubrics_metrics.description: Movement is not made of immobilities; every attempt to reconstitute change out of states implies the absurd proposition that movement coincides with immobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent movement as an indivisible act (or series of indivisible bounds) rather than as a sum of positions. Use language and structure that convey continuity and interior articulation of movement; avoid descriptions that imply things 'are' in each successive point as if they were complete, separate states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect natural articulations of movement
rubrics_metrics.description: All movement is articulated inwardly: it is either an indivisible bound (which may occupy a long duration) or a series of indivisible bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing or depicting motion (e.g., Achilles overtaking the tortoise), follow the natural articulations indicated by experience instead of decomposing motions arbitrarily. Anti-pattern: arbitrary subdivision of motion leading to paradoxical conclusions (Zeno-like absurdities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware that perception condenses change into qualities, forms, and acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception's 'primal function' is to grasp a series of elementary changes under the form of a quality or simple state; the mind condenses many elementary movements into a single instant or quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing lived experience, note that qualities (color, sound, resistance), forms (snapshot 'essences'), and acts (schematic ends) are condensations of continuous change. Use this awareness to either exploit condensation deliberately or to break out of it to convey the flow beneath appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language tends to objectify states (adjectives, substantives, verbs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjectives and substantives symbolize states; verbs, as ordinarily used, also tend to call up motionless plans or points of rest rather than genuine becoming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that grammatical categories favor static representation. To convey becoming, rework syntactic and semantic habits (e.g., favour constructions that foreground process or 'becoming' as a subject: 'there is becoming from X to Y' rather than 'X becomes Y').

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer 'becoming' as subject over misleading subject-predicate constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Saying 'There is becoming from the child to the man' foregrounds the transition as reality, whereas 'The child becomes the man' masks the reality of transition by attributing future attributes to a static subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing about processes, consider grammatical formulations that place the transition/process at the center, preventing the collapse of temporal movement into static subject-predicate relations. Anti-pattern: literal readings of 'becomes' that treat subject and predicate as mutually exclusive static states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the practical origin of the intellect's bias toward ends and rest
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellect represents ends as points of rest because its function is to preside over action: consciousness is typically carried to the end (result) rather than to the movements comprising the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In narrative or analysis, resist the tendency to present only schematic, simplified visions of completed acts; include the felt, interior movement and the 'elementary contractions and tensions' that constitute action when needed to capture lived duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid building transition from pre-posed immutable Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Ancient philosophy posits immutable Ideas (Forms) and then adds a metaphysical 'zero' (matter/non-being) to obtain becoming; this reverses the true order in which movement/transition should be primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start description or theory from movement and transition itself, not from static essences; do not presuppose Forms and then account for change by 'degradation' — instead treat forms as moments born of flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat forms as moments of becoming integrated with extension in time and space
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms (qualities, essences, intentions) are 'stable views' cut out of continuity, but they are essentially extended: they occupy space and time because they are materializations within the flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing a 'form' or 'essence', show how it is inseparable from the temporal and spatial extension that produced it; avoid presenting forms as timeless abstractions floating above time.
